posts.name: Paul
posts.cooked:
And, we're back! I apologize for the lack of a post last month; it was one of the things that unfortunately had to be triaged out during the massive pre-Gen Con crush of 80hr work weeks. All of that is behind us though, and things are going fantastically well! Here is a quick summary of things we accomplished in the past two months:

  1. A million different Gen Con things. We're slowly going to be putting videos of all of the panels and our Costume Contest on our YouTube channel. In addition, we sold out of all of the Spirit Island and Lazer Ryderz we brought to the show, and almost sold out of Fate of the Elder Gods in spite of bringing a ridiculous amount
  2. We fulfilled a ton of Kickstarters!
  3. We had a revelation about the organization of the Sentinel Comics RPG line of books (post-Starter Kit).
  4. We sold out of both Spirit Island and Lazer Ryderz at the warehouse level! We already have reprints in the works for these, but the response has vastly exceeded our projections.
  5. We had some awesome meetings about Prime War development at Gen Con.
  6. We made a ton of progress on The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, which will be on Kickstarter in October.

Here is the status of all of our works in progress!

In Stock Since July

  1. Lazer Ryderz
  2. Exoplanets
  3. Spirit Island
  4. Fate of the Elder Gods
  5. A bunch of reprints (Compounded, SotM stuff, etc)

Shipping to Backers

  1. Bottom of the 9th: Clubhouse
  2. Lazer Ryderz playmats

In Transit; On A Boat

  1. Nothing, unusually.

In Mass Production

  1. SotM: Stuntman, Benchmark, & Void Guard
  2. SotM: Complete Hero Variant Collection
  3. SotM: Ultimate Collector's Case
  4. SotM: 5th Anniversary Foil Villain Collection
  5. Spirit Island core game reprint
  6. Lazer Ryderz core game reprint
  7. Various SotM expansion reprints

At Factory; Pre-Press Work

  1. SotM: OblivAeon
  2. Sentinel Comics: The Role Playing Game: Starter Kit
  3. Spirit Island: Branch & Claw reprint

Current WIP Focus by GTG

  1. Sentinel Comics: The Role Playing Game core rulebook (Christopher, Jenn, Critical Hits)
  2. Prime War (Christopher)
  3. Legend of Sleepy Hollow (Chris Kirkman + Jenn)
  4. A new and improved website (Jenn, Paul, Joel, etc) (really for real this year, hopefully)
  5. A cool Sentinel Comics related thing for 2018

I'll see you next month!

posts.cooked: Basically, we had a giant pile of content in addition to the Core Rulebook. We had a number of discussions at Gen Con, both internal and with experienced people in the RPG industry, and it really helped solidify how we want to organize and release that. What you wind up seeing when we launch the Kickstarter for the RPG in ~February will be the result of those conversations and realizations (plus a bunch of detail work we have to do between now and then, of course).

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Makes sense.  The RPG market hasn't been consistent about what books go in the "core" product and what go in supplements, and how many books the "core" product consists of.  Some games use the D&D approach of Player's Guide and GM's Guide, then Monsters/Enemies and Settings as supplements.  Some lump the Monsters/Enemies stuff into the GM book, and some lump the Settings stuff into the Players book.  Some just make one massive $100 book.

I would imagine that, given how crucial the setting is to the Sentinels game, and how focused it is on major enemies and disposable mooks and not random encounters with widely varying and fiddly monsters, that there won't be a setting or a "monster" book.  But I'd guess, with not much confidence, that there will be a separate GM book that will include how to develop and manage villains, other enemies, and environments, as well as campaign structure and rewards.

Unfortunately, I'd also guess that "weird stuff" that isn't part of the core Sentinels experience, like magic, will probably be in supplements.  I know a lot of people want to create Virtuosos of the Void, but I'm guessing that the core book will enable players to create just the hero types from the core SotM game and maybe a handful of others (non-super characters like Expat and Fixer).  But I wouldn't be surprised if they named and mocked up a magic supplement to wave at us for the Kickstarter, because that would help onboard a bunch of fans.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
My imagnation on the book has been that it will be a big book similar to what I've seen for FATE or Star Wars, "everything you need to start goes here" and then the following products will narrow down on locations or specific events.

 

I feel like magic and heroes like Expat or Fixer are going to be possible with the base book. As I understand the system it is incredibly modular, with the specific things like "motivational charge" or "Lightspeed Barrage" being pre-made mods to the existing four or five actions in the game.

 

I'm not sure how many examples they will havem or how they will advise building these abilities, that's going to be the biggest kicker in how this game goes over in my opinion, but if the difference between the abilities is whether you attack with the highest and hinder with the lowest or vice versa, then saying your power source is magic vs guns vs martial arts vs flames isn't a huge deal. And that gets covered before you get to that point of the character creation, as I understand it.

 

Honestly, as excited as I am for the game, seeing and understanding character creation is going to be a massive challenge, in my experience. It's one of the reasons I'm twitchy about running everything, because as the DM/GM/ whatever you call it, you need to be the one who can answer most of the questions. And character creation is almost always the hardest part of the game.

 

 

 

Turning away from that discussion for a moment

 

OMG OMG OMG, things are printing and getting prepared at the Presses. WOOT WOOT WOOT :D
